subject: Math
prompt: A line intersects two parallel lines, forming four acute angles and four obtuse angles. The measure of one of the acute angles is $(5x - 290)^°$. The sum of the measures of one of the acute angles and three of the obtuse angles is $(-10x + w)^°$. What is the value of $w$?
explanation: The correct answer is $1120$. When a transversal line intersects two parallel lines, it forms eight angles: four acute angles that are all congruent to each other, and four obtuse angles that are all congruent to each other. Additionally, each acute angle and each obtuse angle form a linear pair, meaning they are supplementary and their measures sum to $180^{\circ}$. Given that one acute angle measures $(5x - 290)^{\circ}$, each obtuse angle measures $180^{\circ} - (5x - 290)^{\circ} = 180 - 5x + 290 = (-5x + 470)^{\circ}$. The sum of one acute angle and three obtuse angles is: $(5x - 290) + 3(-5x + 470) = 5x - 290 + 3(-5x) + 3(470) = 5x - 290 - 15x + 1410 = -10x + 1120$. Since this sum is given as $(-10x + w)^{\circ}$, matching the expressions gives $-10x + 1120 = -10x + w$, so $w = 1120$.
